assumptions: The review is read-only and covers the supplied P11 plan plus current repository interfaces.
P11 remains bounded engineering evidence and does not claim accounting validity, forecast validity, or human authoring superiority.
checks: Inspected the mission requirements and confirmed MC23, MC25 and MC31 require shared-task comparisons, concrete adapter contracts, version evidence and explicit limits.
Inspected Core 0 frontend/compiler interfaces and P03 tests; the proposed DSL and typed-constructor comparison can share IR and runtime.
Audited the plan for baseline validity, proxy promotion, vetoes, unfair comparisons, hidden defaults, environment mismatch and artifact sufficiency.
Confirmed the P11 output directory and required test/deliverable files are currently absent, so this review evaluates the plan rather than implementation.
issues: The plan does not include the required material default/assumption audit. Its assumptions list names the interpreter, dependency policy, DemoDebt conventions and read-only status, but does not record provenance, justification, failure mode, earliest diagnostic and promotion status for material choices such as the interpreter/environment, CPU-only execution, subprocess timeout, rounding/calendar conventions, QuantLib tolerance, no-download policy and adapter-selection rules. Add this audit to the pre-edit step and preserve it in the phase record before any integration or numerical check runs.

The ledger backend is not selected reproducibly: 'prefer Beancount ... or explicitly identify an available Ledger/hledger backend' leaves the implementation environment-dependent. Predeclare a deterministic candidate order and discovery rule, record all candidate statuses, and require the selected backend's exact version/location, command or API, unit/calendar conventions and actual exchange. If all are unavailable, record that outcome explicitly rather than selecting opportunistically.
next_actions: Revise the P11 plan to add the complete default/assumption audit and deterministic ledger-backend selection rule.
Then execute the existing bounded implementation steps, keeping unavailable external tools unavailable and preserving the stated vetoes and nonclaims.
residuals: A successful P11 run would still provide bounded engineering evidence only; broader G2/G9 closure, professional accounting validity, empirical forecast validity and human acceptance remain open.
Arelle, ACTUS, QuantLib, Docling and ledger integrations may remain unavailable in the inspected environment; no unavailable tool may be represented as completed integration.
steps: Retain the proposed shared DemoDebt runtime, independent rational oracle, matched DSL/typed inputs, poison-expected-values test, adapter exchange records and explicit result-status separation.
Before implementation, amend step 1 with the required assumption audit and backend-selection rule; no other material plan change is required.
summary: The P11 plan has a sound bounded baseline, shared-runtime comparison, adapter-record schema, negative checks and explicit nonclaims. It requires revision before execution to satisfy the mandatory default/assumption audit and to make ledger-backend selection reproducible.
